Reporting to the Senior Director of Human Resources, this role is responsible for providing practical HR guidance with a strong focus on employee relations, talent acquisition, and leadership support while ensuring consistent HR practices across a growing organization. This position is ideal for an experienced HR professional who enjoys balancing strategic partnership with hands-on execution. The HR Manager works closely with physicians, practice administrators, operational leaders, and corporate stakeholders to address employee concerns, support organizational growth, recruit top talent, and foster positive workplace cultures while respecting the unique identity of each practice. Success in this role requires sound judgment, exceptional relationship-building skills, strong business acumen, and the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced, evolving organization. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Employee Relations & HR Partnership Â Serve as the primary HR partner to assigned business leaders, physicians, and practice administrators, providing practical guidance on employee relations, performance management, organizational policies, and HR best practices. Handle employee relations matters from initial intake through resolution, including conducting workplace investigations, documenting findings, and recommending appropriate corrective actions. Coach leaders through difficult conversations, performance concerns, conflict resolution, employee engagement, and policy interpretation. Balance employee advocacy with sound business judgment while minimizing organizational risk. Identify employee relations trends and recommend proactive solutions to strengthen leadership effectiveness, improve retention, and enhance workplace culture. Build trusted relationships with leaders across multiple locations while supporting the unique culture of each independent practice. Talent Acquisition & Workforce Planning Partner with hiring managers to identify staffing needs and develop recruiting strategies for clinical, administrative, and corporate positions. Manage full-cycle recruitment including sourcing, screening, interviewing, offer coordination, and hiring. Collaborate with recruiting resources and hiring leaders to improve candidate experience and reduce time-to-fill. Coordinate and support onboarding to ensure new employees successfully integrate into both the organization and their individual practice culture. Assist leadership with workforce planning to support organizational growth, expansion, and acquisitions. HR Operations & Organizational Support Provide day-to-day HR support to assigned practices and NSO leaders. Support organizational growth initiatives, including onboarding new practices and assisting with HR integration efforts. Assist in developing scalable HR policies, procedures, and best practices that support a decentralized operating model. Partner with Payroll, Benefits, HRIS, Compliance, and Operations to ensure a consistent and positive employee experience. Ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local employment laws, company policies, and regulatory requirements. Leadership & Organizational Effectiveness Build credibility and trusted partnerships with leaders at all levels of the organization. Support organizational change initiatives through effective communication, coaching, and employee support. Use data, sound judgment, and business insight to help leaders make informed workforce decisions. Participate in HR initiatives that improve employee engagement, retention, leadership capability, and operational effectiveness. Travel Travel up to 20% to partner practices and regional locations to provide on-site HR support, conduct investigations, facilitate training, and strengthen relationships with practice leadership. Qualifications Education Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, or a related field required. Experience 5+ years of progressive Human Resources experience. Experience supporting multiple locations or business units preferred. Previous experience in healthcare, physician practice management, National Services Organizations (NSOs), or similarly complex environments is strongly preferred. Demonstrated experience managing employee relations matters and conducting workplace investigations. Hands-on full-cycle recruiting experience required. Preferred Certifications SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, or SPHR certification preferred. Knowledge, Skills & Abilities The ideal candidate will: Â Demonstrate strong expertise in employee relations and conflict resolution. Think strategically while remaining willing to execute day-to-day HR responsibilities. Build strong relationships and credibility with leaders across the organization. Effectively coach managers on performance management, employee development, and workplace concerns. Possess strong recruiting skills with the ability to identify and attract high-quality talent. Thrive in a fast-paced, growing environment where priorities evolve quickly. Exercise sound judgment, discretion, and professionalism when handling confidential information. Ability to communicate effectively through speaking, listening, and reading. Occasional reaching, stooping, kneeling, or crouching. Ability to lift, push, pull, or move up to 10 pounds on an occasional basis. job.title: Data Analyst Assistant
job.jdText: We are adding a Data Analyst Assistant to the team to support a large scale engagement with an established Italian infrastructure group. This position focuses on interrogating financial assumptions and identifying discrepancies in complex portfolios to ensure our partner makes decisions based on hard evidence rather than corporate narratives. About Blue Oak Consulting Blue Oak Consulting provides independent advisory on pricing, portfolio economics, capital allocation, and acquisition assumptions. We are not a traditional consulting firm focused on broad transformation programs or high level strategy decks. Instead, we interrogate specific commercial decisions where the financial stakes are high and the existing narrative is not sufficient. Our team looks past corporate language and P&L complexity to identify where value is leaking or capital is trapped. We work across sectors like software, manufacturing, and healthcare to test whether the assumptions behind a growth plan or an acquisition actually hold under pressure. We are a small, principal led firm where the people who do the work are the ones accountable for the results. We do not take transaction contingent fees, which allows us to be completely honest about whether the economics of a decision make sense. Our goal is to provide clarity through financial discipline and a healthy amount of skepticism. The Role This is a full time, permanent position that is conducted entirely in a remote environment. You will work closely with our principals to dig into the numbers provided by our partners, often starting with the Italian infrastructure project. The goal is to move past P&L complexity and find where value might be leaking. You will be expected to think critically and ask why certain numbers exist high up in a spreadsheet, rather than just accepting them as facts. This role offers an attractive and competitive compensation package for an entry level professional looking to gain deep experience in financial analysis. What You Will Be Doing Cleaning and organizing large datasets from various sources to build a clear financial picture. Testing the logic behind pricing assumptions to see if they survive real world friction. Helping build financial models that track capital allocation across different infrastructure assets. Identifying outliers and anomalies in expenditure reports that do not align with the stated narrative. Updating portfolio economics trackers to reflect new acquisition data. Collaborating with the team through virtual channels to clarify findings and refine analysis. Preparing clear summaries of data trends that highlight potential financial risks. Verifying the accuracy of inputs used in growth forecasts for specific business units. Assisting in the interrogation of acquisition assumptions for new investment opportunities. What You Bring A degree or background in finance, economics, mathematics, or a related field with a heavy emphasis on data. Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including the ability to manage complex formulas and large tables. A skeptical mindset that enjoys finding inconsistencies in spreadsheets and reports. Comfort working in a fully remote setting where communication is largely written and specific. Ability to organize messy data into structured formats without losing important context. Interest in how large businesses actually spend money and allocate internal capital. Reliability and a willingness to learn how to scrutinize financial statements at a deep level. Strong attention to detail, especially when reviewing line items that seem out of place. What We Offer A fully remote work schedule that provides flexibility and removes the need for a daily commute. Direct access to firm principals who provide mentorship and clear feedback on your work. The opportunity to work on high stakes projects, such as our current work with the Italian infrastructure group. A professional environment focused on logic and evidence rather than corporate politics. Practical training in financial modeling and capital allocation analysis. A permanent, stable role within a firm that values individual accountability and results. At Blue Oak Consulting, we believe that clarity comes from discipline and a healthy amount of skepticism. We stay through the execution phase of our projects because we know that decisions looking sound in theory often face challenges once they meet reality. This role is a starting point for someone who wants to understand the mechanics of how value is created and protected in large organizations. We value the work over the performance, and we look for assistants who are eager to show how the numbers actually add up without relying on corporate jargon.
